desc:
The array nums is arranged on a circle: after the last element comes the first one again. Each query is a pair [start, length]. It asks for the sum of length consecutive elements read clockwise from index start, wrapping around the end of the array as often as needed (a length larger than n goes around the circle more than once).

Return the answer of every query, in order.

nums = [3, -1, 4, 1, 5]
[1, 3]  -> -1 + 4 + 1 = 4
[3, 4]  -> 1 + 5 + 3 + (-1) = 8
[0, 12] -> two full laps (24) + 3 + (-1) = 26
result = [4, 8, 26]
hints: Simulating each query costs O(length). With long queries and many of them that is far too slow.
A query of length L contains L // n complete laps, each worth exactly the total sum of the array, plus a leftover of L % n elements.
Build a prefix sum array pre. The leftover starts at start and may wrap: if start + rem ≤ n it is pre[start + rem] - pre[start], otherwise it is pre[n] - pre[start] + pre[start + rem - n].
editorial: Split the query into whole laps and a remainder: laps, rem = divmod(length, n). The laps contribute laps * total. The remainder is a window of rem < n elements beginning at start. If it does not cross the end of the array (start + rem ≤ n) it is an ordinary prefix-sum difference. Otherwise it is the tail from start to the end plus the head of length start + rem - n, each of which is a prefix-sum difference as well.
Preprocessing is O(n) and each query O(1), so the total is O(n + q). The largest possible answer is 100,000 × 1,000 = 10<sup>8</sup> in absolute value, which fits in 32 bits.
